title: A 232-to-260GHz CMOS Amplifier-Multiplier Chain With a Low-Cost, Matching-Sheet-Assisted Radiation Package and 11.1dBm Total Radiated Power
problem: Compact CMOS terahertz (THz) sources are limited by low radiated power (several mW); on-chip radiation via front-side patch antennas suffers low efficiency (~25%) and narrow bandwidth (~5%); back-side radiation improves efficiency but requires expensive silicon lenses (cm-sized, high-cost assembly) to overcome total internal reflection at Si-air interface.
motivation: 6G communications, THz imaging, molecular spectroscopy, and compact integrated clocks demand chip-scale THz radiation sources with watt-level power in compact packages. Existing solutions are either low-power (front-side) or expensive/bulky (back-side with lenses).
method: The chip contains an amplifier-multiplier chain operating at 232–260 GHz in CMOS technology. It radiates the signal out the back using a patterned dielectric matching sheet instead of expensive silicon lenses—this thin layer transitions waves from silicon's high permittivity (εr=11.9) to air's low permittivity (εr=1), preventing the signal from bouncing back and improving radiation efficiency and bandwidth. The circuit uses high-power FinFET transistors and broadband power amplifiers designed for strong gain across the frequency range.
key_novelty: A patterned dielectric matching sheet replaces expensive silicon lenses for efficient terahertz radiation out the back of a CMOS chip, enabling low-cost packaging.
contributions: 232–260GHz CMOS amplifier-multiplier chain with 28GHz bandwidth (12% fractional bandwidth)
11.1dBm total radiated power (peak, watt-level at load, orders-of-magnitude vs. prior CMOS THz sources)
Matching-sheet-assisted back-side radiation (planar, low-cost vs. lens assemblies)
Broadband gain-peaking power amplifier in CMOS HyPowerFF technology
Direct antenna/load coupling without cm-sized lens
baselines: Front-side patch antenna CMOS THz sources (25% efficiency, 5% bandwidth, mW power)
Back-side with silicon lens (high cost, cm-scale, bulky)
limitations: Abstract does not provide absolute radiated power in watts, gain, efficiency metrics (PAE), or spectral purity (phase noise, harmonics). Matching-sheet design/optimization not detailed.
primary_theme: Low-cost CMOS terahertz source via matching-sheet radiation
